qa_rejections_7d.notes: A routine VIP tandem jump: no danger, no rescue, and about a third of the runtime is cabin interviews and harnessing. Fails the viral bar; no reshuffle of shots fixes that.
Same air station, same Nantucket basket hoist and same overhead angle as ccf-20261115-12, with grainier, color-smeared footage; it would look interchangeable.
Source is one 29 s clip with a single drop; after the splash about 15 s is a static floating capsule, and nothing is at risk.
Source is heavily compressed with color noise through the whole hoist, and it is the fourth near-identical Coast Guard medevac hoist in this batch; footage cannot be fixed.
Calm seas, routine basket hoist of a seated elderly man whose face is on screen during a medical emergency (stroke signs); fails the viral bar and the no-medical-scenes rule.
Very noisy low-bitrate footage, patient strapped in a litter, routine hoist with no visible danger.
Clean airshow formation B-roll but no danger, no turn and no stakes; the outcome is just flying back to base. Below the viral bar and in the review's do-less routine bucket.
Low-resolution, purple-tinted ISS TV feed with a dark, near-empty opening frame and a repeated shot at 32 to 34 s; nothing visibly goes wrong. Interchangeable with today's sharper HD spacewalk (02).
Every shot is the same white cloud mass from orbit, with no visible turn and no landfall footage; hurricane content is in the review's do-less list and the hazards lane is the weakest.

Clean high-speed liftoff but no danger, no turn, and the capsule is cropped out of most frames; it is interchangeable with the many launch Shorts already queued (shuttle, Artemis, Columbia) and 08 tells a stronger launch story.

Calm training dive with no danger on screen; about six seconds of blurry water-on-glass close-ups in the middle and a static hatch shot. The Squalus history is a good idea but the footage cannot carry it.

Hoist-cam footage is smeared with heavy color noise and the top-down frames are hard to read in the first second; a third Kodiak Jayhawk hoist in this batch, interchangeable with recent Alaska hoists.
Artemis II liftoff again (already 14-03, 14-32, 16-08 in the queue or posted), and about ten seconds in the middle show a tiny rocket sitting on the pad before ignition.
Calm routine hoist: the hoist cam hangs over a small patch of deck for most of the Short, mostly in a narrow fit strip, and the 964-foot ship is never shown at scale.
The release does not say how the night ended, so the outcome line is unsupported; one locked shot for 25 seconds and the fifth lava fountain Short in the queue.
